classification.classification_note: The fix commit describes a double free, but the reproduced failure is a heap-use-after-free WRITE because the second `DH_free` first decrements the freed object's refcount in `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF` before any second `OPENSSL_free(r)` can occur.

bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is a 465-byte TLS transcript (sha256 `ceab833db2000d7605e89d2caa4768a3d6ac556d662c4d4c98bfbfd62de8f04b`). In the saved vulnerable run, the `client` fuzz target feeds those bytes into `SSL_do_handshake()`, the handshake reaches `tls_process_key_exchange()`, and the DHE `ServerKeyExchange` body is dispatched into `tls_process_ske_dhe()`. `PACKET_get_length_prefixed_2()` slices that body into `prime`, `generator`, and `pub_key`; `BN_bin2bn()` then materializes them, and the prime's numeric bit length is only 997 because the 255-byte field is mostly zero-filled. The function allocates a `DH`, stores the attacker-controlled fields into it, and then `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` transfers ownership of that same `DH` object into `peer_tmp` without clearing the local `dh` alias. The immediately following `ssl_security()` call computes `EVP_PKEY_security_bits(peer_tmp)` as 0, so under the harness's `@SECLEVEL=0` temporary-DH keys below 80 bits are rejected and the function jumps to `err:` with `SSL_R_DH_KEY_TOO_SMALL`. That cleanup first calls `DH_free(dh)` and then `EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp)`, whose DH ameth callback calls `DH_free(peer_tmp->pkey.dh)` again. The second `DH_free` decrements the refcount inside already freed memory, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 4 at `include/internal/refcount.h:51` in `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF`. The staged patch fixes this by setting `dh = NULL` immediately after `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` and then calling `ssl_security()` with `EVP_PKEY_get0_DH(peer_tmp)` instead of the stale local alias.

source.description: First project parser step that slices the attacker-controlled `ServerKeyExchange` body into the DHE `prime`, `generator`, and `pub_key` packet views later turned into the doubly-freed `DH` object.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 465 bytes (sha256 `ceab833db2000d7605e89d2caa4768a3d6ac556d662c4d4c98bfbfd62de8f04b`). At file offset 66 it contains a TLS handshake record `16 03 03 01 8a`; its `ServerKeyExchange` body starts at offset 75 and the three length-prefixed vectors consumed here are `prime_len = 0x00ff`, `generator_len = 0x0001`, and `pub_key_len = 0x0080`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled TLS transcript first becomes vulnerability-relevant when these helpers expose the three DHE vectors that determine the later `DH` fields, its computed security bits, and the aliased cleanup path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The same staged 465-byte witness drives all three packets. The parsed values later become a 997-bit `p`, a one-byte generator `0x32`, and a non-zero peer public key.

root_cause.description: Successful `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH` transfers DH ownership into `peer_tmp`, but the vulnerable code leaves the local `dh` alias live, so the later weak-key error path frees both aliases.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `dh = NULL;` immediately after this call and changes the following `ssl_security()` call to use `EVP_PKEY_get0_DH(peer_tmp)`, removing the second owner from the shared cleanup path.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The second `DH_free` decrements the refcount stored in the already freed `DH` object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 4` here with crash stack `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF -> DH_free -> evp_pkey_free_it`, after the same `DH` allocation was first freed from `tls_process_ske_dhe:2179`.

parser_admitted.description: The earlier handshake state resolves `algorithm_mkey` to the DHE branch, so the attacker-controlled `ServerKeyExchange` body is dispatched into `tls_process_ske_dhe()`.

post_assignment_failure.description: After `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` succeeds, this is the only remaining `goto err` in `tls_process_ske_dhe()`. The saved free stack at `tls_process_ske_dhe:2179` therefore proves the vulnerable run took this post-assignment weak-key rejection edge.

fine_trace.note: Source. `PACKET_get_length_prefixed_2` slices the attacker-controlled `ServerKeyExchange` body into three packet views. On the exact 465-byte witness, those vectors are `prime_len = 255`, `generator_len = 1`, and `pub_key_len = 128`; this is the first project statement that materializes the DHE fields later converted into the aliased `DH` object.

`EVP_PKEY_new()` allocates the owner container and `DH_new()` allocates the zeroed `DH` object that ASan later identifies as the freed 176-byte region. Because `DH_new()` uses `OPENSSL_zalloc`, the new object starts with `q == NULL` and `length == 0`.

The three packet slices are converted into owned BIGNUMs. On the exact witness, the prime's numeric bit length is 997 because the 255-byte field is mostly zero-filled, `g` is the one-byte value `0x32`, and `bnpub_key` is non-zero, so the later `BN_is_zero` guard does not abort.

`DH_set0_pqg` transfers the attacker-derived prime and generator into `dh` and leaves `q == NULL`. Because the fresh object's `length` is still 0, the later DH security-strength calculation will be derived directly from `BN_num_bits(dh->params.p)`.

The structurally-invalid parameter cases are absent on the saved path: `DH_check_params` succeeds and leaves `check_bits == 0`, so parsing continues even though the group is still too weak for the later temporary-DH security policy.
The non-zero attacker public key is moved into the same `dh` object. At this point the DH allocation contains all attacker-chosen field state that will be aliased into `peer_tmp`.

Root cause. `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH` succeeds and, through `EVP_PKEY_assign`, stores the same `dh` pointer into `peer_tmp->pkey.ptr`, transferring DH ownership to `peer_tmp`. The vulnerable code does not clear the local `dh` alias, so both names now refer to the same allocation on the later error path. The staged patch fixes this by setting `dh = NULL` here.

The post-assignment temporary-DH check computes `EVP_PKEY_security_bits(peer_tmp)` through the DH helpers. With `q == NULL`, `length == 0`, and `BN_num_bits(p) == 997`, `DH_security_bits` reaches `BN_security_bits(997, -1)` and returns 0; under the harness's `SSL_set_cipher_list(client, "ALL:eNULL:@SECLEVEL=0")`, `ssl_security_default_callback` rejects `SSL_SECOP_TMP_DH` when `bits < 80`. This branch therefore raises `SSL_R_DH_KEY_TOO_SMALL` and jumps to `err:` after ownership already moved into `peer_tmp`.

The shared cleanup first frees the local alias. Because step 7 never cleared `dh`, this call drops the only `DH` object's refcount to zero and reaches `OPENSSL_free(r)`; the saved ASan free stack names `tls_process_ske_dhe:2179` and `DH_free:148` as the free context.

The next cleanup call `EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp)` reaches `evp_pkey_free_it`, whose DH ameth free callback is `int_dh_free`. It passes `peer_tmp->pkey.dh` to `DH_free`; that field still contains the same pointer freed in step 9.

Sink. The second `DH_free` from step 10 re-enters `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF` with `val` pointing at the freed `DH` object's `references` field, and this atomic decrement writes 4 bytes into freed memory. ASan reports `heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 4` here with crash stack `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF -> DH_free -> evp_pkey_free_it`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch sets `dh = NULL` immediately after `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` succeeds and then calls `ssl_security(..., EVP_PKEY_get0_DH(peer_tmp))`, so the `err:` block no longer double-drops the same `DH` allocation through both `dh` and `peer_tmp`.

format.name: exact 465-byte TLS DHE `ServerKeyExchange` transcript with a 997-bit prime
format.contract: Exactly the staged 465-byte witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_20816/poc` (sha256 `ceab833db2000d7605e89d2caa4768a3d6ac556d662c4d4c98bfbfd62de8f04b`). At file offset 66 it contains a TLS handshake record whose `ServerKeyExchange` body begins with the length-prefixed DHE vectors `prime_len = 255`, `generator_len = 1`, and `pub_key_len = 128`. On the saved path, `PACKET_get_length_prefixed_2()` materializes those vectors, `BN_bin2bn()` turns the prime into a 997-bit BIGNUM, `EVP_PKEY_security_bits(peer_tmp)` therefore becomes 0, and the post-assignment `ssl_security()` call takes the `SSL_R_DH_KEY_TOO_SMALL` error path after `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` has already transferred ownership. The trigger semantics recorded here do not generalize beyond this exact staged transcript.
